report_topic: the Efficacy of Implementation of Seventy-fourth Constitutional Amendment Act in Maharashtra
observations_summary: The audit found that while all 18 functions were devolved to Urban Local Bodies (ULBs) as per the 74th Constitutional Amendment Act, several functions were also performed by parastatal agencies, diluting devolution. ULBs faced issues with institutional arrangements, financial resources, and human resources, leading to poor service delivery in water supply, sanitation, and fire services. Key findings include delays in constituting the State Finance Commission and implementing its recommendations, low property tax collection efficiency (53% overall, 28% in MCGM), and significant short disbursements of various grants (Additional Stamp Duty, Nagarpalika Sahayak Anudan, Pilgrim Tax, Road Grant). There was a 31% shortfall in manpower in test-checked ULBs and a 61% shortage of fire stations. Service Level Benchmarks for water supply and sewage services were largely not met, with low water connection coverage, inadequate per capita supply, lack of metering, and poor water quality and sewage treatment.
